_: Award ceremonies that are one body split across two Wikidata items: Wikidata files some of the body's prizes under its organisation (P1027, conferred by) and others under its 'Awards' group, so the facts stage finds both. The store build files `from` under `into` before building the ceremony table. A festival merges into the festival; an academy whose one ceremony is a prize merges into the prize, the name a viewer searches for. The Emmys (Primetime, Daytime, International) are separate ceremonies and stay apart. See store/awards.py.

merges.why: National Board of Review Awards is the National Board of Review's own awards group; its prizes are filed half under each (138 and 768 titles)
Venice Film Festival Awards are the Venice Film Festival's prizes (79 and 87 titles)
the Silver Bear is a Berlin International Film Festival prize; the Golden Bear already files under the festival (78 and 106 titles)
Cannes Film Festival Awards are the Cannes Film Festival's prizes; a few are filed under the festival itself (203 and 4 titles)
the Gouden Kalf is the Netherlands Film Festival's prize, which files the rest of its awards under the festival (22 and 33 titles)
the Spanish film academy's one ceremony is the Goya Awards (1 and 118 titles)
the Catalan film academy's one ceremony is the Gaudí Awards (10 and 42 titles)
